decisions.directMechanism: A qualifying controlling public agency using ordinary FAA approval or the statutory streamlined notice route may collect one of$1/$2/$3/$4/$4.50 for eligible airport projects or their debt service. Charges are capped by boardings/trip and subject to passenger exemptions. Revenue authority is project-specific; collection approval does not prove completed construction, demand change or general local tax permission.

Farm and airport exemptions/limits require separate handling; County153A-277 separately permits fees outside municipalities with parallel hearing, cost and overlapping-program limits. Bona fide farm uses and military runways/taxiways are exempt; other airport runway/taxiway exemption requires specified reinvestment and certification.

Effective August 28, 2008; complete January 2026 amendment comparison and affirmative local grant remain unverified. Helper-read official text; lead retrieval failed.

bars.description: Certificate-covered telecommunications restriction with express service exceptions.
bars.changedBy: State legislature amends the cited restriction. Local actors may exercise express statutory exceptions; no independent local repeal or referendum waiver established.

MT.scope: own-place statutory restriction, service scope and express exceptions
MT.reason: Government ISP operation is generally barred, including through another subdivision. Exceptions cover no available private ISP, service before July 1, 2001, or advanced services unavailable privately. A private entrant triggers notice; government may choose to discontinue within 180 days, rather than being required to withdraw. Digital government services, purchased Internet access, funding private broadband, and contiguous-campus infrastructure remain permitted. History through 2025 chapter 53 section 5; exact 2025 effective date and complete cutoff comparison remain unverified. Lead independently read 2025 text.

bars.description: General ISP restriction subject to specified service and grandfather exceptions.
bars.changedBy: State legislature amends the cited restriction. Local actors may exercise express statutory exceptions; no independent local repeal or referendum waiver established.

NE.scope: own-place statutory restriction, service scope and express exceptions
NE.reason: Non-public-power governmental entities generally may not provide retail or wholesale broadband, Internet, telecommunications or video services. Listed educational/statutory exceptions and authorized service already provided before January 1, 2005 are preserved. Sections 86-575 through 86-577 concern conditional dark-fiber transactions, which differ from telecommunications service. Public-power entities require separate 86-595 review; exclusion from this restriction is not a retail grant. History lists 2005 LB645 and 2021 LB384. Lead independently read 86-594; complete cutoff comparison remains unverified.

bars.description: Retail/wholesale service restriction with specified statutory and existing-service exceptions.
bars.changedBy: State legislature amends the cited restriction. Local actors may exercise express statutory exceptions; no independent local repeal or referendum waiver established.

NV.scope: own-place statutory restriction, service scope and express exceptions
NV.reason: Incorporated cities with population at least 25,000 generally may not sell telecommunications service to the public; airport exception. Covered facility construction crossing public rights-of-way requires a cost-benefit study, public-interest finding and public inspection. Helper inspected definitions in 704.025/704.028; no express Internet or cable exception found there. County scope and affirmative smaller-city authority remain unverified. Section history: 1997 addition, 2007 amendment; current chapter revision is September 2026, not an archived January snapshot.

decisions.question: Should the principal utility commission use public elections or appointments, and how should its nomination and confirmation route work?

examples.measure: Constitutional Amendment1 submitted November3,2020; ArticleXI section1 transitions to three appointed members January1,2023

AL.scope: state-level change to principal commission selection
AL.reason: Existing selection evidence is recorded in topic authorities where available; the power and constitutional/statutory route to change it have not been completely researched.

AK.scope: ordinary-statute replacement of constitutional regulatory-board appointment
AK.reason: Published ArticleIII26 requires gubernatorial appointment and joint legislative confirmation for a board heading a regulatory or quasi-judicial agency. A statute alone cannot replace that constitutional route with public election; the current RCA-specific statutory consolidation remains incomplete.

bars.description: Constitutional appointment and confirmation requirement for regulatory agency boards.
bars.changedBy: ArticleXIII1: two-thirds of each legislative house proposes amendment for next general election; majority of proposition votes adopts. Convention/revision is a separate route and not researched here.

AZ.scope: ordinary-statute replacement of constitutionally required public election
AZ.reason: ArticleXV section1 requires elected commissioners. Replacing that selection rule requires constitutional amendment under ArticleXXI section1, rather than ordinary legislation.

bars.description: Constitutional public-election requirement for principal commission membership.
bars.changedBy: Majority of each legislative house or qualifying15-percent initiative petition submits amendment; voter majority ratifies an ordinary amendment. Tax-approval amendments have a separate60-percent rule.

federalLink.match: Regulatory jurisdiction boundary; not a matching grant or uniform cost share.
conditions: Wholesale means resale under section201(d). Interstate transmission and jurisdictional wholesale rates are federal; retail rates are not ordinarily set by FERC.
Section201(f) excludes listed governmental and cooperative entities from ordinary PartII regulation unless a provision specifically reaches them; exceptions prevent a blanket municipal exemption.

The statute compilation is through2018 amendments;2025 agency guidance corroborates the core boundary. Later amendments, specific preemption cases, ERCOT and territorial exceptions still need consolidation.

verification.promptClaim: 3. **Local taxes for transportation need state permission.** Local-option sales taxes for transportation are allowed in many states but not all. Some need voter approval (California: two-thirds for a special tax, under Proposition 13 and Proposition 218, lowered to 55% for some measures; **verify** current thresholds). Availability belongs on each place's fiscal-authority record (the game has `92N_NATIONAL_STATE_LOCAL_FISCAL_AUTHORITY`).
verification.finding: Proposition 5 would have lowered some local infrastructure bond approvals to 55%; official 2024 results rejected it. Do not apply 55% to transportation special taxes. Citizen-initiative special taxes and school bonds require separate legal classification.

verification.promptClaim: - **State, then local:** revenue sharing of fuel tax and registration fees by formula (the formula is a state setting); state preemption of local speed limits (varies: some states let cities set 20 or 25 mph by ordinance, and Oregon and Washington expanded this, **verify**); state approval of local tolling.
verification.finding: The marked Oregon/Washington expansion claim is verified: Oregon2017 Portland residential grant expanded to all cities2019; current eligible residential reduction up to10mph with20mph floor. Washington20mph nonarterial/10mph shared streets have separate procedures and state-highway approval. Neither is universal county power. Revenue-sharing formulas and toll routes remain separate research work.

verification.promptClaim: 1. **Fuel tax rate, and indexing it to inflation.** State. About 22 states index or vary their rate (**verify** count, ITEP). Effect: gasoline demand elasticity about -0.05 to -0.1 short run, -0.3 long run (Hughes, Knittel and Sperling 2008; Brons and others 2008). Revenue falls about 0.84% a year as fuel economy rises (already in the game). Available in every state and D.C.; territories set their own. Local fuel taxes are allowed in about 12 states (**verify**).
verification.finding: ITEPJuly2025 and NCSLMay2025 report26states+DC but mix current/future designs: COindexingFY2032–33, WAfirst2% adjustmentJuly2026, MSindexingJuly2029 after fixed steps. January2026 active-index count unresolved. HKSshort-run2001–06 range−.077 to−.034; Bronsmeta mean−.34 short/−.84 long, not claimed−.3. Full-text ranges/horizons unverified, so no Brons runtime coefficient admitted.

verification.promptClaim: 1. **Fuel tax rate, and indexing it to inflation.** State. About 22 states index or vary their rate (**verify** count, ITEP). Effect: gasoline demand elasticity about -0.05 to -0.1 short run, -0.3 long run (Hughes, Knittel and Sperling 2008; Brons and others 2008). Revenue falls about 0.84% a year as fuel economy rises (already in the game). Available in every state and D.C.; territories set their own. Local fuel taxes are allowed in about 12 states (**verify**).
verification.finding: Current nationwide local fuel-tax count remains unresearched;2009 count cannot establish2026 law. Gasoline-price elasticity contrast corrected in item1; tax transfer needs retail-price pass-through and tax share, not direct substitution.

verification.promptClaim: 3. **Electric vehicle registration fee.** State. More than 30 states charge one, typically $50 to $200 a year. Effect: a small drop in electric vehicle sales (**verify** study).
verification.finding: Jenn2018 fixed-effects observational model reports0.24% lower EV sales per$1 enacted fee over2010–June2018 data. Implementation coefficient is smaller and statistically nonsignificant. This is study-specific, not universal causation. January2026 fee count remains unresolved. NCSLJuly2026 reports at least42states and35hybrid-fee states but includes future NM2027 and NJ2028 schedule amounts. Primary NM2026 act confirms delayed2027 start; primary NJMVC schedule exceeds$200 already byJan2026. This survey is not an active-Jan2026 count. Own-state primary batch establishes ten more enacted fee routes; KSJanuary2026 passenger165/100/70 are category fees,not extra charges. KY2026adjustment and OKcombined collectible total unresolved; COadjustedbase production retrieval unverified. National active-fee count remains unresolved.

verification.promptClaim: 4. **Tolling and congestion pricing.** State law must authorize it, and federal approval is needed on federal-aid highways (the Value Pricing Pilot Program). Example: New York's Manhattan central business district tolling, which started January 5, 2025, at $9 a car at peak. Effect: traffic entering the zone fell about 7 to 11% in the first months (MTA reports, **verify**), with transit ridership up. Available only where state law authorizes it.
verification.finding: MTA reports 11% fewer zone entries over its first six months of 2025. This is an observed program comparison, not a universal causal coefficient. Initial peak car toll was$9 and launchJanuary 5,2025.

verification.promptClaim: 7. **Complete streets and Vision Zero rules.** State and city. More than 1,700 complete-streets policies nationwide (Smart Growth America, **verify**). Effect: pedestrian deaths down where speeds drop; a lower speed limit of 20 mph cuts pedestrian fatality risk sharply (AAA Foundation, Tefft 2011).
verification.finding: SGA2025 report verifies more than1700 adopted policies; older1600 page was stale. Tefft2013 links impact speed to conditional pedestrian death risk, not direct effect of lowering a posted limit. No automatic policy-to-fatality coefficient admitted.

verification.promptClaim: 8. **Automated speed and red-light cameras.** State law authorizes or bans them, and cities deploy them. About 20 states ban or limit speed cameras (IIHS, **verify**). Effect: red-light cameras cut fatal red-light crashes about 21% in large cities (IIHS 2011).
verification.finding: Canonical September2026 IIHS speed rows explicitly list prohibitions inID,ME,MS,NH,NJ,TX,WV,WI; SC generally prohibits with emergency exception. No-law rows are not bans; permitted systems may have narrower site limits. About20 lacks a defined category.2011 fatal red-light study24%,2016 study21%.

verification.promptClaim: - **Special district:** most transit is run by an authority (for example SEPTA, MARTA, King County Metro, which is a county department, and Denver RTD), with board seats appointed by member governments or elected (Denver RTD's board is elected, **verify**).
verification.finding: RTD states it has 15 publicly elected directors. King County Metro is a county department, not evidence that every transit operator is a special district.

verification.promptClaim: - **Member governments:** board appointment shares and a cost-sharing formula; a member may withdraw where state law allows it (Michigan towns opted out of SMART, **verify**).
verification.finding: SMART2020 records historical community opt-in/out. Oakland2022 countywide millage removed former gaps. PA236/2024 enactedJanuary17,2025 effectiveApril2,2025 amends withdrawal124.458;>=1.1m-county exclusion/all-member trigger follows expiration of millage then in force. Existing obligations survive; current universal local opt-out claim is wrong.

verification.promptClaim: 4. **Bus lanes and signal priority.** City. Effect: bus speeds up 5 to 15% (NACTO, **verify**).
verification.finding: NYCDOT reports14thStreet pilot maxima24% speed/30% ridership, which does not verify a generic NACTO5–15% range. Original monitoring tables and comparable counterfactual remain unverified; no universal numerical effect admitted. Rootdownloaded/readNACTOMoveThatBus,p28–29:dedicated-lane summary gives10–25%travel-time reduction,notprompt5–15%speedrange. ReferencesincludeNYCadvocacyrelease,TriMetown2019case andFTA2010BRTreport;notall-place causalcoverage. OriginalNYCmonitoringretrieval remains403; do notsubstitutepublishercaserangefornationalanchor.

verification.promptClaim: 7. **Transit-oriented zoning near stations.** State and city. Example: California SB 79 (2025) allows height near transit (**verify** passage). See Zoning.
verification.finding: SB 79 approvedOctober 10,2025 asChapter 512. Local applicability generally beginsJuly 1,2026; other provisions have different schedules.

verification.promptClaim: **Availability:** local transit taxes are barred where state law doesn't enable them. Some states give no dedicated local option (**verify** list, APTA).
verification.finding: Own-place FL,WA,NC,TX conditional transit/transporttax grants and TN pre-cutoff Davidson implementation now established. WA overlappingentity bars,TXconfirmation/ratecaps andNCeligiblegeography are route-specific,not statewideprohibitions. INprimarydated text,APTAexhaustive nationalbarlist andJanuary2026fullcomparison remainunresearched.

verification.promptClaim: 1. **Fund or drop a state-supported Amtrak route.** State. It carries an annual appropriation. Examples: Virginia's Transforming Rail in Virginia (2019 to 2021, bought rail right of way, **verify**); Indiana funded, then ended, the Hoosier State (2019).
verification.finding: Virginia2020 authority law and2021 CSX acquisition verified. INDOT identifies funding loss and final Hoosier State runJune30,2019; federally supported Cardinal is a separate service.

verification.promptClaim: - Effect: route ridership. Virginia's routes grew strongly after frequency was added (**verify** figures). Road trips shift, and emissions fall per diverted trip.
verification.finding: VPRA management discussion reports FY2024 ridership1,384,665 and FY2025 ridership1,451,276. This section is unaudited. The increase alone does not identify frequency effects; a harmonized2015–2025 corridor panel remains unresolved.

verification.promptClaim: - Availability: every state may fund it. Old "internal improvements" clauses once barred state railroad investment (Michigan 1850, Wisconsin 1848). Wisconsin later amended its constitution to allow transportation appropriations (**verify** the year and article), and Michigan funds its routes through its transportation fund. **Research: each state's current constitutional credit, gift and internal-improvement clauses as they apply to rail.**
verification.finding: Wisconsin ArticleVIII§10(2)(e) rail appropriation exception and§7(2)(a)1 debt authority were addedApril1992; highway exception1908 and ports1960 are separate. Proposed general transportation amendment was rejected1975 and1976. Historical primary text resolves year/article; live official consolidation and nationwide clause matrix remain gaps. Official2023 LRB text corroborates the rail exceptions without removing VIII3 private-credit bar. MichiganIII6 permits legislatively provided public improvements; IX18/19 credit/equity limits remain distinct. MinnesotaXI5(i) permits capped railway rehabilitation debt; Maine7155 explicitly bars direct state operation for chapter acquisitions. Some Michigan evidence is indexed official text with direct reads unavailable; full2026 and nationwide review remain incomplete.

verification.promptClaim: 2. **Create and fund a high-speed or new intercity rail authority and bond.** State. Example: California Proposition 1A (2008). Effect: capital spending and jobs; ridership only when a segment opens. Cost overruns are common (Flyvbjerg: rail projects overrun about 45% on average, **verify**).
verification.finding: Prop1A bond authorization was2008, outside required example window. SB1029 Chapter152/2012 appropriated already-authorized bond proceeds; use it as an appropriation example, not new bond authorization. No ridership or construction-cost causal coefficient admitted.

verification.promptClaim: 3. **Short-line freight rail tax credit or grants.** State: Georgia, Oregon, Alabama and others (**verify** list). Federal: the 45G credit, made permanent in 2020. Effect: track upgraded to 286,000-pound cars keeps freight off roads and lowers road damage (**verify** size).
verification.finding: Oregon HB2164/2019 and Alabama HB457/2019 credit examples verified. Georgia HB588/2021 concerns freight grants/P3 authority, not proof of a short-line tax credit. Exhaustive state list, road-damage size remain unresearched; federal45G permanence is resolved in item2. Primary evidence adds MN2023/2025, MO2026 (eligible2027; agency implementation2028), WIAct242 signed2026, OK2020/2023 amendments and KS2022. Utah comparable maintenance credit remains unverified. This bounded seven-state set is not an exhaustive count.

verification.promptClaim: 3. **Short-line freight rail tax credit or grants.** State: Georgia, Oregon, Alabama and others (**verify** list). Federal: the 45G credit, made permanent in 2020. Effect: track upgraded to 286,000-pound cars keeps freight off roads and lowers road damage (**verify** size).
verification.finding: PL116-260 divisionEE§105 removed45G expiry in2020. Credit is40% for tax years starting2023 onward,50% before2023, capped at$3500 per eligible mile with assignment restrictions. Road-damage effect remains unsized.

verification.promptClaim: 8. **Buy right of way from freight railroads for passenger use.** State. Virginia bought track from CSX in 2021 (**verify**).
verification.finding: Virginia acquired specified corridor interests through 2021 CSX transaction; first phase closedApril 2021. Do not read an old planned opening date as present service.

verification.promptClaim: 9. **Two-person crew rules.** State laws were contested; the FRA issued a federal rule in 2024 requiring two people. State rules stand only where they aren't preempted (**verify**).
verification.finding: FRA 2024 crew rule upheld by Eleventh CircuitAugust 11,2026. Contains exemptions; state regulations cannot be assumed freely additive. Subsequent appeal docket not checked.

verification.promptClaim: 5. **Port and airport minimum wages.** Owner and city. Examples: SeaTac's Proposition 1 (2013), $15; Los Angeles airport concession wages. Effect: wages and headcount for airport workers (**verify** studies).
verification.finding: Original airport wage studies are located and scoped: SFO2003 reports observed wage/turnover changes under bundled policies; headcount growth is not causal jobs creation. LA2005 reports affected positions across contract sectors but excludes LAX from control comparisons. SeaTac projected6300/72 is coverage; no SeaTac-specific causal wage/headcount coefficient admitted.

verification.promptClaim: 6. **State aviation fuel tax use.** State. Federal rules require it be spent on aviation since 2014 (**verify**).
verification.finding: FAA 2014 policy clarified application to aviation fuel taxes, including general sales tax revenue attributable to aviation fuel. Statutory obligations predate 2014; transition/enforcement and grandfather exceptions matter.

verification.promptClaim: - **Federal:** the Safe Drinking Water Act sets enforceable maximum contaminant levels, a **federal floor**, and states run it with "primacy". Examples: the 2024 limits on PFAS chemicals, and the 2024 Lead and Copper Rule Improvements, which require replacing lead service lines within about 10 years (**verify** the status after 2025 changes). The Clean Water Act sets wastewater discharge permits (NPDES), which most states administer. State Revolving Funds are **conditional spending**, with a 20% state match.
verification.finding: LCRI final 2024 rule remains published with general compliance beginning 2027 and replacement timetables/exceptions. EPAJuly 2026 page describes PFOA/PFOS requestable 2031 compliance extension and other PFAS rescissions as proposed, not finalized.

verification.promptClaim: - **State:** primacy agency; the utility commission regulates **investor-owned** water utilities' rates; state law on privatization. **Fair-market-value laws** in about 15 states (for example Pennsylvania's Act 12 of 2016, **verify** count) let private utilities buy public systems at appraised value, which raises customer rates.
verification.finding: NARUC 2021 review lists 12 enacted-policy states; Florida added a 2023 law. These 13 named states across dated evidence do not establish an exhaustive 2026 count. Rate consequences need study-specific sizing. Florida2025 codification establishes the optional eligible-acquirer process and PSC review; an enacted acquisition valuation route does not itself establish a causal bill increase. Original May2024 Cornell thesis independently reports thirteen states asof2024; this is not the final journal article or exhaustive January2026count. NC and Iowa own statutes now establish bounded valuation routes; no universal causal rate-increase coefficient follows. Virginia2020,OhioAugust2025,MissouriAugust2025 and Kentucky2021 own statutes now distinguish commission valuation safeguards. Kentucky has net-original-cost/acquisition-price treatment rather than assumed three-appraisal FMV classification; exhaustive count remains open. Illinois2021enactment andTexas2019enactment plusagencyadoption establish two further bounded routes; full January2026amendment history andexhaustivecount remain open. Indiana own2025regulator confirms acquisition route and2024/2025amendments; its price averages are not causal rate effects. Thirteen historical named states now have bounded own-place evidence,but exhaustive January2026classification andamendment histories remain incomplete.

verification.promptClaim: - **State oversight of local rates:** varies. In most states it covers only investor-owned utilities, but some states regulate municipal utilities serving outside city limits (**verify** list).
verification.finding: WisconsinPSC regulates municipal drinking-water rates. verification.finding: Missouri Zweig2013 required approval for the particular impervious-area assessment. California SB231/2017 adds stormwater to statutory sewer definition;2022 Department of Finance ruling addresses pre2018 law and nonretroactivity, not invalidation. verification.promptClaim: - **State:** broadband office, grant programs, **limits on municipal broadband**. About 16 states restrict public networks (BroadbandNow 2024, **verify**). North Carolina's HB 129 (2011) is an example.
verification.finding: NC retains conditional network/accounting/debt restrictions and individual exemptions. ArkansasAct67/2021 expanded government authority with financing conditions; Act412/2025 did not undo it. Tennessee municipal-electric authority is territory-limited with exceptions; full current exception geography not retrieved. Colorado2023 and Washington2021 expanded permission. No nationwide16-state count adopted. RootreadMinnesota2025and2024enactment:former65%telephoneexchangevoterequirementremoved;Internetgrant nowconditionalnondiscrimination/separation. Six further own-place restrictions are recorded with exceptions: MO Internet-type exclusion, MT availability/grandfather routes, NE non-public-power scope, NV population-qualified city scope, PA incumbent request route, and SC provider conditions. These cannot support a uniform prohibition label or a January 2026 national count.

verification.promptClaim: **Effects:** broadband availability raises employment and property values modestly (Kolko 2012; Whitacre and others 2014, **verify** sizes).
verification.finding: Kolko2010 employment result is historical association.
